entities.name: Query RibBA protein
observations: 423 aa protein with strong homology to reviewed bacterial RibBA bifunctional riboflavin-biosynthesis proteins.
Sequence contains DHBP_synthase Pfam domain at residues 9-199 and GTP_cyclohydro2 domain at residues 207-364.
Closest reviewed homologs show 54.4-57.9% identity over approximately 92% query coverage.
Predicted molecular mass is 44.67 kDa and theoretical pI is 5.47.

entities.name: D-ribulose-5-phosphate DHBP synthesis
observations: RibBA catalyzes conversion of D-ribulose 5-phosphate to (2S)-2-hydroxy-3-oxobutyl phosphate, also called 3,4-dihydroxy-2-butanone 4-phosphate, with formate produced.
Annotated as EC 4.1.99.12 and Rhea RHEA:18457 in reviewed homologs.

entities.name: GTP cyclohydrolase II reaction
observations: RibBA catalyzes GTP conversion to 2,5-diamino-6-hydroxy-4-(5-phosphoribosylamino)-pyrimidine, formate, phosphate, and protons; the product is also described as DARP/ DAROP in annotations.
Annotated as EC 3.5.4.25 and Rhea RHEA:23704 in reviewed homologs.

entities.name: Riboflavin biosynthesis
observations: The two RibBA activities provide the first committed steps of riboflavin biosynthesis: DHBP formation from ribulose-5-phosphate and GTP cyclohydrolase II formation of the pyrimidine precursor.
Reviewed homologs associate both activities with cytosolic riboflavin biosynthesis.
